# Stage 8 report (DiffCoTune "ours" and paper variants; generated by `make_report8.py` 17 Nov 2026 11:16 from the result files; parts 1–4 are `report_stage8_part*.md`)

## 1. Paper settings (DiffCoTune, Krishna et al. 2025) and DiffTune facts

Source: `docs/papers/krishna2025diffcotune.pdf` (read only, text extracted page by page, PDF pages 1–8) and the summary `docs/papers/summaries/krishna2025diffcotune.md`. Page numbers are the PDF page numbers.

### 1.1 DiffCoTune (arXiv 2505.24068v1), verbatim or near-verbatim

| Setting | What the paper states | Page |
|---|---|---|
| Task cost | "c(x_t, x_t*) := ‖x_t − x_t*‖₂², where x_t* is the desired state at time t. For states that evolve in different geometric spaces (e.g., position in R³ and quaternions in S³), we compute an unweighted sum of the individual cumulative norm squared errors." J_task(θ, β) = (1/T) Σ c(x_t, u_t), eq. 5 | 3, 4 |
| System-identification cost | J_sysId = (1/T) Σ ‖x_t − x_t^sys‖², closed-loop states of simulator and target under the same controller, eq. 3 (same unweighted sum over state parts) | 3, 4 |
| Update strategy used | Split-Alternate: β first (θ fixed), then θ in the updated simulator, "a maximum of K/2 epochs for both the β and θ updates" (Alg. 3) | 4 |
| Optimiser | Adam [42] "for computing the gradient update in Alg. 2 and 3"; Optax [45]. **Learning rate: not stated** (the text only says "identical design choices (learning rate and maximum epochs, K) as the combined variant" in the ablation) | 4 |
| Epochs | "We take K = 100" (so K/2 = 50 per inner loop) | 4 |
| Stop rule | termination condition C := 1(\|J_k − J_{k−1}\| < 10⁻³) ∨ 1(J_k > J_{k−1} + 10⁻³), "to terminate under convergence or divergence due to unbounded updates"; units of J: those of the cost as defined (no normalisation stated) | 4 |
| Iterations on the target | "limit to a single rollout in the target system per iteration and maximum tuning iteration of L = 5"; Alg. 1 loops l = 0 … L (= 6 rollouts) | 3, 4 |
| Weights | Combined variant only: w_task = w_sysId = 1; "refrain from setup-specific tuning" | 4 |
| Sensor noise in the tuning | **Not mentioned.** The word "noise" appears only in the introduction (uncertainties from "unmodeled dynamics, noise") and in the quadruped hardware experiment (noisy velocity feedback filtered with a 5th-order Savitzky–Golay filter on the hardware) | 1, 5 |
| Trust region | **Not mentioned** | – |
| Projection | Biped MPC: θ = entries of diag(Q); "we add a clipping operator to our gradient update (like [27]) to project θ into a feasible set (Q ⪰ 0)" | 5 |
| Keep-best | Alg. 1: θ_best replaced when J_task(θ_best, sys) ≥ J_task(θ_{l+1}, sys) — needs the real cost of θ_{l+1} | 3 |
| Other | one gain set per task; no quadrotor example (Table I); JAX / MJX / Flax / Optax; no repeated seeds reported | 4 |

### 1.2 DiffTune (Cheng et al., IEEE T-RO 2024) — ANOTHER PAPER, not DiffCoTune (same group, quadrotor hardware)

Pages are those of `docs/papers/cheng2024difftune.pdf`. These are facts about DiffTune only; none is a DiffCoTune setting.

| Setting | DiffTune | Page |
|---|---|---|
| Update | projected gradient descent θ ← P_Θ(θ − α ∇θ L) (plain gradient descent in raw gain units, not Adam) | 5 |
| Hardware trust region | "learning rate α = 0.1 together with gradient clipping such that each update is within 10 % of the current parameters θ_j, i.e. θ_{j+1} ∈ [0.9 θ_j, 1.1 θ_j]" | 11 |
| Hardware loss | L = ‖p − p̄‖² + tr(I − R̄ᵀR)/2 (position + attitude), horizon 7 s | 11 |
| Hardware budget | 10 trials | 11 |
| Sensor noise in its simulations | zero-mean Gaussian noise added to the simulation (std position 0.1 m, velocity 0.1 m/s, rate 1e-3 rad/s per the summary) | 9 |
| Learning rates compared | 0.1 / 0.01 / 0.001 (Fig. 14: faster with larger α, oscillation at 0.1); simulation runs with α = 0.01 and up to 50 trials | 13, 14 |
| Claim | "learning rate as the sole hyperparameter" (p. 10, their statement) | 10 |

DiffTune's learning rates are for plain gradient descent on raw gains and do not transfer to our Adam on log-ratios.


## 2. Why the body rates break J_sysId for us (step 1b; S0, plant P1, true β, default gains, 5 scenarios)

**Error floors per state component** (`results/floors.json`; mean over the sysId window; units p m², v (m/s)², q (unit-quaternion difference)², w (rad/s)²; cells = p / v / q / w and the share of the body-rate part):

| scenario | A: noise-free truth vs noise-free model | B: noisy truth (seed 1) vs noise-free model | C: noisy seed 1 vs noisy seed 2 |
|---|---|---|---|
| A1 | 9.21e-11 / 9.18e-12 / 0 / 0 (w 0 %) | 0.0114 / 0.507 / 0.045 / 10.6 (w 95 %) | 0.0211 / 1.05 / 0.0944 / 23.2 (w 95 %) |
| A8 | 6.76e-10 / 3.3e-09 / 7.24e-12 / 7.74e-09 (w 66 %) | 0.00106 / 0.00617 / 0.000113 / 0.427 (w 98 %) | 0.000351 / 0.00458 / 0.000282 / 0.557 (w 99 %) |
| CIRCLE | 2.85e-11 / 1.1e-11 / 6.68e-13 / 2.33e-09 (w 98 %) | 4.2e-05 / 0.00016 / 1.74e-05 / 0.0586 (w 100 %) | 1.57e-05 / 0.000227 / 3.61e-05 / 0.124 (w 100 %) |
| FIG8 | 2.28e-11 / 1.77e-11 / 8.24e-13 / 2.1e-09 (w 98 %) | 4.07e-05 / 0.000246 / 1.76e-05 / 0.0577 (w 99 %) | 2.95e-05 / 0.000423 / 3.91e-05 / 0.129 (w 100 %) |
| A4 | 1.24e-09 / 8.31e-09 / 2.48e-10 / 4.27e-08 (w 81 %) | 0.00151 / 0.0129 / 0.000551 / 0.262 (w 95 %) | 0.000377 / 0.00422 / 0.000233 / 0.392 (w 99 %) |

A: the noise-free model reproduces the noise-free truth to 1e-10 … 5e-8, so there is no model-mismatch floor at the true β. B and C: against a noisy flight the floor is **95–100 % body rate** in every scenario (A1: 11.2 for one noisy flight against the noise-free model, 24.4 between two noise seeds; the position part is 0.011 and 0.021). The same share holds for the J_sysId parts at the start of the fit (p 0.018, v 0.126, q 0.010, w 2.51 on average over the scenarios, `ident8.json`).

**Phase decorrelation** (`results/floors.json`, `rates`; A1, A8, A4, two noise seeds at the true β):

| scenario | axis | body-rate RMS noise-free truth / noisy 1 / noisy 2 (rad/s) | dominant frequency noisy 1 (Hz) | correlation noisy 1 vs noisy 2 (lag 0 / best, lag) | correlation noisy 1 vs noise-free (lag 0) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| A1 | x | 0.000 / 2.36 / 2.22 | 1.13 | 0.46 / -0.91, -0.57 s | 0.00 |
| A1 | y | 0.000 / 2.16 / 2.28 | 1.13 | -0.60 / 0.87, +0.32 s | 0.00 |
| A1 | z | 0.000 / 0.65 / 0.71 | 0.07 | -0.31 / -0.60, +0.53 s | 0.00 |
| A8 | x | 0.913 / 1.06 / 1.12 | 0.94 | 0.97 / 0.97, +0.00 s | 0.91 |
| A8 | y | 0.000 / 0.47 / 0.30 | 7.67 | -0.45 / -0.45, -0.12 s | 0.00 |
| A8 | z | 0.000 / 0.12 / 0.13 | 7.22 | -0.08 / 0.25, +1.00 s | 0.00 |
| A4 | x | 0.519 / 0.59 / 0.57 | 1.20 | 0.81 / 0.85, +0.02 s | 0.84 |
| A4 | y | 0.413 / 0.59 / 0.58 | 7.60 | 0.66 / 0.67, -0.01 s | 0.77 |
| A4 | z | 0.095 / 0.16 / 0.17 | 7.60 | 0.36 / 0.48, +0.06 s | 0.70 |

On A1 the noise-free truth has body rate 0.000 (a hover hold) while both noisy flights oscillate at 2.2–2.4 rad/s about x and y at about 1.1 Hz; the two noise seeds correlate at 0.46 / −0.60 at lag 0, their best correlation (about 0.9) sits at different random lags (−0.57 s, +0.32 s), and neither correlates with the noise-free truth (0.00). **The A1 rate oscillation is noise-driven (a limit cycle excited by the sensor noise, random phase).** On A8 and A4 the x-rate has a deterministic part (seed-seed 0.97 / 0.81, with the noise-free truth 0.91 / 0.84); the y and z rates are noise-dominated (about 7.2–7.7 Hz).

**Units.** The unweighted sum adds m², (m/s)², a dimensionless quaternion term and (rad/s)². The reference body rates of the scenarios are small (|w*| ≤ 0.26 rad/s by flatness), but the measured rates are 1–2 rad/s: numerically the rate term is about 16 times the sum of the other three (2.51 against 0.154) at the start of the fit.

**Paper-exact identifiability** (`results/ident8.json`; fit only, noisy flights of θ₀ with seeds 0 and 1, lr 0.01, forward gradient, 5 scenarios; truth: thrust 0.8, lag 1.5, downwash 1.3, plume 0.7):

| J_sysId form | β error: thrust gain / motor lag / downwash / plume (%) | epochs (stop) | J start → returned |
|---|---|---|---|
| p+v+q (ours), 50 epochs, best iterate | -6.3 / -56.4 / -35.3 / +64.8 | 51 (max epochs) | 0.1539 → 0.1421 |
| p+v+q+w paper-exact (true body rate of the flight), 50 epochs, best iterate | +0.9 / -30.7 / +20.9 / +14.4 | 51 (max epochs) | 2.662 → 2.448 |
| p+v+q+w paper-exact (true rate), paper stop rule | +7.0 / -31.6 / +14.2 / +17.7 | 45 (converged |dJ| < 1e-3) | 2.662 → 2.471 |
| p+v+q+w, measured gyro (true rate + gyro noise), paper stop rule | +7.6 / -31.7 / +14.8 / +17.7 | 46 (converged |dJ| < 1e-3) | 2.796 → 2.604 |

(Stage 4e, 4 scenarios, p+v+q best iterate: −1.7 / −34.5 / +5.7 / +22.3 %; with the measured gyro in the 4-scenario set it was −11.4 / −37.9 / −16.1 / +39.4 %.)

**Conclusion in plain words.** The body-rate part of J_sysId is almost entirely a noise-driven oscillation that a noise-free model cannot reproduce, so it is 95–100 % of the cost and sets its floor. Even so, in this sim-to-sim identifiability test the paper form (all four parts, unweighted) is **not worse** than our p+v+q: with the true rate of the flight it gives +0.9 / −30.7 / +20.9 / +14.4 % against −6.3 / −56.4 / −35.3 / +64.8 % for p+v+q on the same flights, and the measured-gyro form with the paper stop rule gives +7.6 / −31.7 / +14.8 / +17.7 %. So the body rates do not break the **fit** in this test (the deterministic x-rate parts on A8 and A4 carry information); what fails in the paper variant is the **tuning**: the real cost gets worse with every round (Section 5). Why the paper form works for the paper's systems: its simulations are noise-free sim-to-sim, so the rates are predictable. **Smallest change that keeps the paper form and is robust to the noise: not established**; candidates (proposal, not adopted): a noise model in the simulator with several noise seeds averaged in J_sysId (as the frozen method does for the task cost), or fitting only the deterministic rate part (x-rate on A8 and A4).

**Share of the body rates in the task cost per round and fit epochs per round:** fit and tune epochs per round are in the per-controller tables of Section 5; the share of p, v, q, w in the paper task cost per round (`taskshare.py`) is listed in Section 5 where it was computed (not computed if the line is missing).


## 3. Learning rate (step 1c)

**What is stated.** The DiffCoTune paper does not state the learning rate (p. 4: only "Adam", and "identical design choices (learning rate and maximum epochs, K)" for the ablation). Adam's default is 1e-3 (Kingma & Ba 2015, "Adam: a method for stochastic optimization", recommended α = 0.001; the PyTorch default is also 1e-3). Optax's `adam` takes the learning rate as an argument; whether it has a default was **not checked here**. DiffTune (another paper) compared 0.1 / 0.01 / 0.001 with plain gradient descent on raw gains and used 0.1 on hardware with a ±10 % trust region and 0.01 in simulation; its values do not transfer to Adam on log-ratios. In our parameterisation φ = log(gain / default gain), Adam moves each φ by about lr per epoch when the gradient sign stays the same, so lr 0.01 is at most about 1 % per epoch and at most about 65 % (exp 0.5) in a 50-epoch inner loop.

**Probe** (S0, plant P1, paper variant: full-state task cost, p+v+q+w fit, paper stop rule, no noise, no trust region, forward gradient, 5 scenarios; 3 flown rounds each; the real cost after round 1 is the flight of θ₁):

| lr | real 3-D RMS after round 0 / 1 / 2 (cm) | fit epochs (rounds 0, 1, 2) | tune epochs | largest gain change to next set (rounds 0, 1) | crashes | floor flights per round |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1e-3 | 18.24 / 18.31 / 18.44 | 26, 2, 19 | 50, 50, 10 | 5.7 %, 6.1 % | 0 | 1, 1, 1 |
| 3e-3 | 18.24 / 17.67 / 17.57 | 29, 8, 6 | 50, 30, 17 | 16.0 %, 8.8 % | 0 | 1, 1, 1 |
| 1e-2 | 18.24 / 17.24 / 22.09 | 18, 2, 8 | 14, 41, 7 | 13.8 %, 45.7 % | 0 | 1, 1, 1 |

**Rule** (user): best real cost after round 1 with no crash or floor flight; within 0.3 cm take the smaller lr. Real cost after round 1: 18.31 / 17.67 / 17.24 cm for 1e-3 / 3e-3 / 1e-2 (the default gains give 18.24 cm). No probe had a crash. A1 is a floor flight at the default gains in this dry-run plant in every probe (so the floor criterion does not separate the rates). **Chosen: lr 0.01** (0.43 cm better than 3e-3). Note: at 1e-2 the flight of θ₂ was worse (22.09 cm, largest gain change 45.7 % between θ₁ and θ₂): without a trust region one update can move the gains far; see the safety note.


## 4. RPM delay from real data (step 1d)

* **Where 4.0502 ms comes from.** `simulator/frsim/data/calibration.json` (plant of record, frozen 10 Nov): `rpm_delay_ms` 4.0501500631407525, copied from `experiments/tuning/out/plant_calibration_joint_lag30_best_s0.json`. It is **one of the parameters fitted jointly** to 28 hardware targets (calibration objective 1.40) in the recalibration of 30 Oct 2026 with the motor lag fixed at 30 ms and the other seven parameters re-fitted (`docs/tuning_plant_p4_2026-10-29.md`, update of 30 Oct; before it the fit gave 17.6 ms for a lag of 22 ms). So 4.05 ms is a fitted value of the simulator, not a direct measurement.
* **What was measured on hardware.** (i) `docs/tuning_actuator_id_2026-10-29.md`: command-to-DShot-telemetry delay of the motors from 187 flights, median **6 ms** for S0, S2, S1, S3 and the NS2 / pilot groups, 4 ms for FBL (time constant 30 ms; log resolution 2 ms; the INDI flights fit worse, R² 0.76–0.83); range quoted "4–6 ms". (ii) `docs/43_RPM_Source_Quality.md` and `experiments/analysis/out/rpm_source_quality/`: DShot lags the optical deck by **0–2 ms** (median over 32 motor-rows from 8 flights; typical 0–5 ms; 2 ms grid at 500 Hz).
* **Which source and filtering the firmware uses.** `indi_gains.rpm_source` = 1 (DShot) since 2026-09-18, chosen for reliability not speed (the deck reported zero on two motors in two-drone flights); a spike guard in `rpm_get_all()` since 2026-09-29; the INDI part filters a_rpm, a_imu, τ_rpm and the angular acceleration with a 2nd-order Butterworth, 30 Hz (`s1_model.py`, from `controller_omar_indi.c`).
* **Consistency.** The model's `rpm_delay_ms` is the delay of the rpm signal the INDI sees against the true motor force; the measured 4–6 ms command-to-telemetry delay (with the 30 ms lag in front) is the same kind of quantity. 4.05 ms lies at the lower edge of the measured 4–6 ms. What is **not** measured: the optical deck's own delay, and the exact DShot processing delay inside the firmware (only the relative lag deck–DShot, 0–2 ms, is). The dry-run plant truth of 8 ms (P1RD) is an assumption of the plan, not data.
* **Proposal (the user decides):** 4.05 ms stays: it is consistent with the data (4–6 ms), and moving it to 6 ms (the median of the actuator identification) would change a value that was fitted jointly with the other plant parameters without refitting them.

## 6. Safety note, safety preview, resource incident

**Facts from the dry runs (frsim, nothing flown).** No dry-run flight crashed. A1 is a *floor* flight at the default gains in this dry-run plant (37 cm 3-D error: the plant P1 has thrust 0.8 and motor lag 45 ms against the model's calibration), so every round of every run has at least one floor flag from A1; the floor flags beyond A1 are the signal. Paper S0: floor flights in A1 (all rounds) and A1, A8, A4 in round 5; largest gain jump per round 14 %, 46 %, 6 %, 3 %, 4 %. Paper S2: 2 %, 7 %, 34 %, 6 %, 1 %. "Ours" is limited to ±25 % per round and reaches the limit (S0 ours: 25 % in rounds 0–2). A lab session sees up to 3 attempts per flight (the first plus at most 2 repeats, protocol): a crashed, tilted or floor flight is repeated and not used for the fit.

**S0 "ours" round 3 (15.96 cm).** The flight of round 3 uses θ₃, computed at the end of round 2 (fit 727 s, tune 764 s, normal times); the slowness of the *fit of round 3* (3899 s, during the overload) came after that flight and did not change θ₃ or the real cost of round 3 (the computation is deterministic). What happened in round 3: A1 got worse (15.85 → 34.45 cm, a floor flight) while the other four scenarios improved (A8 8.60 → 6.56, CIRCLE 2.92 → 2.58, FIG8 2.99 → 2.62, A4 8.67 → 5.49 cm); the largest gain change to θ₃ was 25 % (the limit; factors to θ₂: 1.05, 1.24, 1.13, 1.25, 1.25, 1.25, 0.80, 0.90, 0.80, 1.03). The rerun of the S0 "ours" dry run (clean machine) reproduces or not rounds 0–3: see §5.

**Safety preview (`lab/preview.py`, proposal, a check only; never changes the gains).** After the tuning step the new θ is flown in frsim on the 5 tuning scenarios with the round's fitted β, noise on (2 seeds, 2000 and 2001) and the protocol abort rules (crash, tilt > 25° for 0.5 s, z < 0.25 m); the same for the best flown set. FAILED only for abort events the best flown set does not show; the line "NOTE worse" (1.5 × and 2 cm) is information and a proposal, not a rule. Replay on the stored dry-run θ of every round:

| Run | Round | Preview | Real cost of that round (cm) | Reading |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| S0 paper | 1 | PASSED | 17.24 (best before: 18.24) | correct |
| S0 paper | 2, 3, 4 | FAILED (A4 floor, both seeds) | 22.09, 24.33, 24.63 | bad rounds flagged |
| S0 paper | 5 | FAILED (A8 floor) | 30.81 | bad round flagged |
| S0 ours | 1 | PASSED | 9.69 | correct |
| S0 ours | 2 | FAILED (A1 tilt, both seeds) | 9.14 (improved) | false alarm |
| S0 ours | 3 | PASSED | 15.96 (A1 floor) | missed: the model plant (fitted β) is not the true plant |

Time: 110–220 s per preview run serially (20 simulated flights); inside the existing pool workers it takes the time of 4 flights per worker (measured in the first round with the preview: `rep['preview']['seconds']`, target ≤ 2 min). Mock test (`lab/test_preview_mock.py`): the best set as new set gives PREVIEW PASSED; a gain set that crashes in frsim gives PREVIEW FAILED naming scenario, seeds and "crash".

**Resource incident 20:00–21:06 (15 Nov).** Two "ours" dry runs (S0 started 18:38, S2 18:51) ran at the same time. Every pool worker grew to 2.5–2.7 GB resident memory (ten workers, 23 GB; `ps` at 21:03), MemAvailable fell to 0.43 GB with SwapFree 148 kB, and the load average reached 88 / 96 / 101 (1 / 5 / 15 min): both limits (load ≤ 22, MemAvailable ≥ 3 GB) were broken. The second job (S2 "ours") was stopped at 21:04 by exact PIDs (slot script 3056352, job runner 3060169, run script 3060172, and two leftover processes 3060175 / 3060180); memory returned to 12 GB. Touched: S0 "ours" (the fit of round 3 took 3899 s instead of about 730 s; the 45-minute rule then halted the run after round 3) and S2 "ours" (stopped after 2 flown rounds, rerun from scratch). Not touched: the paper S0 dry run ended at 18:02:41 and the paper S2 dry run at 18:13:40, before the second "ours" job began. The finished S0 "ours" process then hung after closing its pool; it was stopped by exact PID 3059119 (its result files were complete). An obsolete background wait loop of Stage 4b was killed by Claude Code under the same memory pressure and not restarted. Since then "ours" jobs run one at a time.
